summary: Preinstall alternate-runtime dropper executes obfuscated payload via downloaded Bun binary
details: @servicetitan/micro-frontend@0.0.4 ships a `preinstall` script (`node setup.mjs`) that runs on `npm install` before user consent. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime v1.3.13 from GitHub releases and uses `execFileSync` to invoke the freshly downloaded Bun binary against a locally shipped 727KB file `math_init.js`. The math_init.js file is heavily obfuscated: a `// @bun @bun-cjs` header followed by a large integer/string constant array (`const n7gIxM=[0x0,0x1,0x8,0xff,...]`) and byte-permutation/string-array rotation routines (`WV8StW`) — Bun-bytecode-obfuscated JavaScript that is not human-inspectable. setup.mjs itself is obfuscated with `_0x`-style renamed identifiers (`_0x488df8`, `_0x52943e`) and dictionary-indirected calls. The package presents itself as a React micro-frontend library, a purpose unrelated to installing an alternate JavaScript runtime and executing an opaque `math_init.js` at install time. The alternate-runtime-dropper pattern deliberately evades Node-based supply-chain scanners that only inspect require()-resolved code. The scope `@servicetitan` is inconsistent with the shipped behavior; the repository field points to a `playground` repository, suggesting scope impersonation or account compromise rather than a first-party release.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
